title: Sharp Tracker and Insider Trading are genuinely separate products — separate routes, cohorts, services, pages and nav entries, with no silent cohort reuse in either direction
claimUnderTest: PR #626 split one feature that shipped under two product names into two products: Insider Trading (league-scoped, cohort = your league-mates, no skill filter) and Sharp Tracker (global, cohort = qualified managers).
observed: The split held. `src/intel/` imports NOTHING from `src/sharp/` (grep: zero import lines). The dependency runs one way only — `src/sharp/{cohort,discovery,market,records,record_queue,roster_collect,roster_store,service,platform_records,roster_percentage}.py` import `src.intel.{ledger,platform_ledger,signals,league_filter}`, i.e. the shared ingestion/metric layer named in the docstring, never a product module. The pools are computed by different functions over different evidence: intel's pool is `service._pool_member_ids(state)` = the keys of the snapshot's `members` dict (this league's managers, no filter); sharp's pool is `cohort.cohort_members()` over `platform_records.build_manager_records` + `score.score_managers`. `market.market_payload` filters every query by `manager_keys` from that cohort. Live: `/api/sharp/market` and `/api/sharp/roster-percentage` return 200 `status:"cohort_building"` with a populated `cohort`/`transparency` block; `/api/intel/summary` returns 503 `data_not_ready`. Nav has two distinct entries (`/market/sharp-tracker` under Market, `/league/insider-trading` under League) and the old `/intel` path is a redirect stub. The Insider Trading page subtitle states the cohort explicitly: 'These are the managers in this league, not a skill-filtered cohort.'

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && grep -rn 'src\.sharp' src/intel/*.py ; grep -rn 'src\.intel' src/sharp/*.py ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/market ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/intel/summary
reproduction.expected: no intel->sharp imports; sharp->intel imports only ledger/platform_ledger/signals/league_filter
reproduction.actual: exactly that; sharp 200 cohort_building, intel 503 data_not_ready

numericProof.formula: count of cross-package import statements per direction

userImpact: None — this is the verified-good case. A user on /market/sharp-tracker is looking at a qualified cohort; a user on /league/insider-trading is looking at their own league-mates and is told so on the page.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding asserts the separation either way; recorded as a verified positive.

whatWorks: The separation is structural, not naming: different pool functions, different evidence tables, different degradation posture, different nav groups, and a redirect on the retired shared path.

title: The ledger's counting rules are correct: multi-team trades, refetches, failed transactions, window overlap and waiver-vs-trade separation all behave as documented under a live numeric probe
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md/src docstrings claim: eventId dedup makes re-ingest a no-op; windows are overlapping lenses never summed; only status=='complete' transactions count; buy/sell counts are TRADES ONLY and waiver/free-agent movements are never inside them.
observed: All four hold when the real `crawler._events_from_tx` + `ledger.ingest_events` + `ledger.asset_signals` are driven with a synthetic transaction set. A 3-team trade (3 players rotating + 2 same-season-same-round picks) produced 10 distinct events with no asset double-counted (each player: buys 1 / sells 1); the two 2027 1sts were kept distinct by the `o<original_roster>` discriminator instead of collapsing. Re-extracting the same transaction with the same seen-set emitted 0 events, and re-ingesting the identical 14-event list inserted 0 movements and 0 transactions. A `status:'failed'` waiver emitted 0 events. FAAB was captured (42) on the waiver ADD only and null on the drop. Trade and waiver queries over the same rows are disjoint: `p1` shows trade buys 1 in the 7d/30d lenses and waiver adds 1 separately, never merged. The 45-day-old trade appears in the 90d lens (p1 buys 2) and not in the 30d lens (p1 buys 1) — the 90d count is a superset, not a sum.

reproduction.expected: three_team_events=10, refetch_events=0, failed_tx_events=0, ingest_second inserted=0, trades_90d[p1].buys=2 vs trades_30d[p1].buys=1, waivers never inside trades_*

numericProof.formula: events = sum over (asset,side) pairs of pool-member participation; window count = COUNT(movements with ts >= now - span)

userImpact: None — the double-counting failure mode the product was audited for in 2026-07 does not occur.

priorFinding.note: Independently re-verifies docs/intel/AUDIT.md section 2 at runtime rather than inheriting it.

whatWorks: Dedup by deterministic eventId at extraction AND at INSERT OR IGNORE; tx_type stored on every movement and TRADE_TX_TYPES / WAIVER_TX_TYPES kept apart at query time; windows expressed as durations with no bucket arithmetic anywhere.

title: The 503 no-data path renders an honest banner AND a fabricated negative in the same view: 'No tracked activity yet — No buy/sell events in the rolling windows'
claimUnderTest: The page comment says a 503 data_not_ready should 'render the "no snapshot" banner state, not an error'.
observed: The 503 handler synthesizes `{assets: [], memberCount: 0, leagueCount: 0, staleHours: null}` and hands it to the normal render path. That produces THREE statements at once in the live DOM: (a) honest — 'No intel snapshot yet — the first crawl hasn't run'; (b) misleading — a subtitle reading 'Trades your league-mates made in their OTHER Sleeper leagues — 0 managers, 0 leagues observed', which reads as a measured zero; (c) fabricated negative — the table area shows 'No tracked activity yet / No buy/sell events in the rolling windows. Check back after the next crawl.' That last sentence asserts an observation the server explicitly refused to make. All the window/sort/direction filter controls also render as if they were operating over data.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W16/w16_page_probe.py  # Playwright, /api/* intercepted to :8000 per AUDIT_PROTOCOL
reproduction.actual: honest banner + '0 managers, 0 leagues observed' + 'No buy/sell events in the rolling windows'

userImpact: A user who scrolls past the amber banner (or who lands mid-page) reads 'No buy/sell events in the rolling windows' and concludes their league-mates have been quiet, when in fact nothing has ever been observed. The two statements contradict each other on the same screen.

priorFinding.note: Prior area A17 has no finding on the 503 empty state.

whatWorks: The 503 is correctly distinguished from an error, and the honest banner IS present — this is a wording/short-circuit defect, not a missing state.
rootCause: The 503 branch returns a normal-shaped empty payload instead of a distinct `notReady` flag, so the generic empty-state copy fires.
requiredRepair: Return `{notReady: true}` from the 503 branch and, when set, render the banner alone — suppress the subtitle counts, the filter bar and the 'No buy/sell events' empty state.

title: The rolling-window limitation is never surfaced: ledger.coverage() is served only to Sharp Tracker, and the board offers a 90-day lens over a ledger whose first-run backfill is capped at 30 days
claimUnderTest: `ledger.coverage()` is documented as existing 'so the UI can say "across the leagues and window available to us" instead of implying global Sleeper coverage'.
observed: No `/api/intel/*` payload contains it. `ledger.coverage` has exactly two callers and both are Sharp Tracker (`src/sharp/service.py:60`, plus roster_store's own coverage). The summary payload's key set, captured from a live in-process run, is {assets, countedTxTypes, eventCount, generatedAt, leagueCount, leagueKey, memberCount, season, sort, staleHours, truncatedMemberCount, window, windows} — no earliestObservedTs, no retentionDays, no coverageNote. Meanwhile the crawler's first run for a league backfills at most BACKFILL_MAX_WEEKS=6 / BACKFILL_MAX_DAYS=30 (crawler.py:53-54) and steady state fetches only the current week (+ previous for 48h), while the UI offers a '90 days' button and the API additionally allows window=all. On a newly crawled league the 90-day view is arithmetically a 30-day view wearing a 90-day label, with nothing on screen saying so. The only coverage caveat the page does render is the 25-league per-member cap note (PER_MEMBER_LEAGUE_CAP=25).

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W16/w16_service_probe.py  # see hasCoverageBlock; then: grep -rn 'ledger.coverage' src/ | grep -v pycache
reproduction.expected: summary payload carries a coverage block; ledger.coverage has an intel caller
reproduction.actual: hasCoverageBlock=false; the only ledger.coverage caller is src/sharp/service.py:60

userImpact: A user switches the board to '90 days', sees the same (or barely different) counts as the 30-day view, and concludes trade interest in a player is flat over a quarter — when two thirds of that quarter was never observed. Nothing on the page distinguishes 'no trades' from 'not crawled'.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and extended: the prior finding stops at 'no route serves coverage()'. The live consequence is the 90d/all lenses over a 30-day first-run backfill, which is the 'partial window presented as history' failure.

whatWorks: `ledger.coverage()` already computes the right fields (earliestObservedTs, retentionDays, movementsByTxType, coverageNote, complete:false), and `truncatedMemberCount` already surfaces the 25-league cap.
rootCause: Coverage was wired into the sharp service only; the intel payload builders were never updated when the read path moved to the ledger.
requiredRepair: Add `ledger.coverage(conn=...)` (pool-filtered) to `build_summary_payload`/`build_player_payload` and render 'observed since <date>' plus a warning when the requested window starts before `earliestObservedTs`.

title: The Insider Trading board counts trades made INSIDE the user's own league while the page states the trades happened in their OTHER Sleeper leagues
claimUnderTest: Page subtitle: 'Trades your league-mates made in their OTHER Sleeper leagues'. `ledger.manager_asset_activity` even provides an `exclude_league_ids` parameter documented as 'removes the league the user is asking about'.
observed: `build_summary_payload` calls `ledger.asset_signals(user_ids=pool, ...)` with no league filter and no exclusion — `asset_signals` has a `league_ids` include parameter but no exclude, and the exclusion that does exist is only on `manager_asset_activity` (the member route). Runtime proof: a synthetic snapshot with one trade in the HOME league and one in an AWAY league puts BOTH assets on the board (`homeLeagueTradeOnBoard: true`). So a trade the user themselves participated in, in this very league, is re-served to them as league-mate intelligence from elsewhere.

numericProof.formula: board_rows = COUNT(DISTINCT asset) over movements WHERE user_id IN pool (no league predicate)

userImpact: A user reads 'three managers bought this player elsewhere' when one of those buys is the trade they made with a league-mate last week inside this league. Their own revealed preference is fed back to them as independent market evidence, and `uniqueManagers`/`uniqueLeagues` — the breadth terms that drive confidence and signal strength — are inflated by it.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with a runtime reproduction against the real build_summary_payload rather than by code reading.

whatWorks: The pool filter itself is correct — the board is scoped to this league's managers, so no other league's activity leaks in.
rootCause: `asset_signals` was given an include-league filter but the summary path passes none, and the home league id is available in the league config but never threaded down.
requiredRepair: Either add `exclude_league_ids=[league_cfg.sleeper_league_id]` to the summary/player queries, or change the subtitle to 'in this and their other Sleeper leagues' and label the home-league share. The former matches the stated product.
dependencies: Blocked-by-data for a production-scale measurement: no snapshot exists in this container.

title: GET /api/intel/member/{ownerId} reports tradeCount as the sum of per-asset trade counts, so a single 3-player trade is reported as 3 trades
claimUnderTest: The payload field is named `tradeCount` and sits beside `movementCount`, whose comment says the unit is deliberately named 'so it cannot be confused with transactions'.
observed: `trade_count = sum(r['tradeCount'] for r in rows)` where `rows` are per-ASSET aggregates. Each asset row's own tradeCount is a correct COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id) for that asset, but summing across assets counts one transaction once per asset it touched. Runtime: one trade in which uA sends p1+p2 and receives p3 is reported as `tradeCount: 3`.

reproduction.actual: reportedTradeCount == 3 (movementCount 3, three asset rows of tradeCount 1)

numericProof.formula: reported = SUM over assets of COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id per asset); correct = COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id)

userImpact: No user impact today — the route has zero frontend consumers (see W16-F007) — but any consumer would over-report a manager's trade activity by roughly the mean assets-per-trade, i.e. 2-4x.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with a runtime reproduction; adds the exact inflation factor (assets-per-trade) and the fix location.

whatWorks: `movementCount` is honest, and the per-asset `tradeCount` values are individually correct.
rootCause: An aggregate that is only valid per-asset is summed across assets.
requiredRepair: Add a `COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id)` query at the manager level (the ledger already indexes `idx_mv_user_ts` and `idx_mv_tx`) instead of summing the per-asset column.

title: Waiver/FAAB activity is fully modelled, ingested and served — but GET /api/intel/waiver-interest and GET /api/intel/member/{ownerId} have zero frontend consumers, so the adds/drops half of the product is unreachable
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE-adjacent docs and the route docstrings claim waiver/free-agent activity 'is served separately by /api/intel/waiver-interest so a claim can never render as a buy'.
observed: The schema DOES distinguish them properly: `transactions.tx_type` and `asset_movements.tx_type` carry trade|waiver|free_agent, `faab_bid` is stored on the winning waiver add (verified: 42 on the add, null on the drop), and `build_waiver_interest_payload` renames buys/sells to adds/drops and strips `net`/`buyRate` because 'net adds is not a meaningful waiver concept'. That work is real and correct. But no page or component fetches it: `grep -rn 'waiver-interest|intel/member' frontend/app frontend/components frontend/lib` returns nothing. The only intel consumers are `/api/intel/summary` and `/api/intel/player` (insider-trading page + PlayerPopup) and `POST /api/intel/leads` (InsiderLeads). So waiver/FAAB is Implemented-but-disconnected, not Missing — and the insider-trading page offers no way to see the adds/drops the crawler is paying Sleeper calls to collect.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && grep -rn 'waiver-interest\|intel/member' frontend/app frontend/components frontend/lib --include=*.jsx --include=*.js ; echo "exit=$?" ; PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W16/w16_ledger_probe.py | head -30
reproduction.expected: at least one frontend fetch of each route
reproduction.actual: grep exit=1 (no matches); the waiver data exists in the ledger and is correctly separated

numericProof.formula: count of distinct /api/intel/* paths appearing in a frontend fetch()

userImpact: A user cannot see which league-mates are spending FAAB on whom — the single most actionable waiver signal the crawl collects — because there is no UI for it. They may also assume the board's silence about waivers means no waiver activity was observed.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed by grep over the frontend tree; adds the schema-side verification that the data behind those routes is genuinely modelled (so the correct label is disconnected, not missing).

whatWorks: The trade/waiver/free-agent split is enforced at the query layer by TRADE_TX_TYPES vs WAIVER_TX_TYPES, and the waiver payload deliberately refuses to emit a `net`. FAAB bids are captured on the add side only.
rootCause: The routes shipped ahead of their UI.
requiredRepair: Add a 'Waivers & FAAB' tab to /league/insider-trading backed by /api/intel/waiver-interest, and link member names on the board to the member profile.
dependencies: W16-F006 should be fixed before the member route gets a consumer.

title: The drill-down 'verify the count' receipts are hardcoded to the 30-day window, so under a 90-day board they list half the movements the headline number counted
claimUnderTest: The receipts block is commented as satisfying 'allow a transaction detail list so users can verify the count'.
observed: `build_player_payload` fetches movements with `signals.window_bounds(signals.INSIDER_DEFAULT_WINDOW, ...)` — always 30d — and the frontend fetches `/api/intel/player?playerId=` with no `window` parameter, so the board's active window never reaches it. Runtime: a player with one trade 3 days ago and one 45 days ago shows `board_90d_volume: 4` on a 90-day board while the drill-down returns 2 movement rows. The expandable summary reads 'N underlying trade movements — verify the count', which is exactly the reconciliation the user cannot perform.

numericProof.formula: receipts = COUNT(movements WHERE ts >= now-30d); headline = COUNT(movements WHERE ts >= now-90d)

userImpact: A user who opens the receipts to audit a 90-day count finds fewer rows than the number printed above them and reasonably concludes the board is wrong (or that movements are missing). The exposure sentence directly above IS labelled 'in the last 30d', which partially mitigates but also puts two different windows in one panel.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with numbers; partial correction — the exposure line IS window-labelled ('in the last 30d'), so the defect is the unlabelled receipts list under a differently-scoped headline, not a wholly unlabelled panel.

whatWorks: The payload stamps its own `window` field and the exposure sentence renders it, so the information needed to fix this is already on the wire.
rootCause: `/api/intel/player` accepts no window parameter and the client sends none.
requiredRepair: Accept `window` on /api/intel/player (allow-listed like the summary route), pass the board's active window from MemberExposure, and label the receipts list with it.

title: signals.sample_confidence's documented calibration is unsatisfiable: it claims ~0.09 at one observation and ~0.86 at twelve, while the constant produces 0.167 and 0.706
claimUnderTest: 'Volume at which sample-size confidence reaches ~0.5. Tuned so a single observation is visibly weak (~0.09) and a dozen is strong (~0.86) without a hard cutoff.'
observed: With `_CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME = 5.0`, `sample_confidence(1) = 1/6 = 0.1667` and `sample_confidence(12) = 12/17 = 0.7059`. Neither matches the stated tuning, and the two targets are mutually unsatisfiable for any single constant: 0.09 at v=1 requires half=10.11, while 0.86 at v=12 requires half=1.95. So the docstring does not describe a previous constant either — it describes a curve this functional form cannot produce.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -c "from src.intel import signals as s; print(s.sample_confidence(1), s.sample_confidence(12), s._CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME)"

numericProof.formula: confidence(v) = v / (v + half); half required for c: half = v(1-c)/c

userImpact: Indirect: `sample_confidence` multiplies into `signal_strength` and feeds `confidence_tier`, which is the label that is supposed to stop a one-observation signal reading like a real one. A single observation scores nearly double the documented weakness, so thin signals are less discounted than the module claims. Shared with Sharp Tracker.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and strengthened: the prior calls it a docstring mismatch; the arithmetic shows the stated pair is unreachable for ANY half-volume, so the intended calibration was never implemented rather than merely drifted.

whatWorks: The saturating form itself is sound and monotone, and `confidence_tier` is emitted alongside every signal.
rootCause: Docstring written against an intended calibration that the chosen functional form cannot satisfy.
requiredRepair: Decide the real target (a single observation should probably score <0.1), pick the constant that produces it, and pin it with a test asserting the docstring's numbers.

title: asset_movements.counterparty_user_id is never populated by the intel crawler, so 'who traded with whom' is structurally unanswerable despite the column, the platform-ledger derivation and the docs promising it
claimUnderTest: The ledger schema carries `counterparty_user_id`, `asset_movements_for` returns it as `counterpartyUserId`, `platform_ledger` derives `counterparty_manager_key` from it in a trigger and a backfill, and FFPC_UNIFIED_SHARP.md lists 'counterparty' as a trade-row field.
observed: `crawler._events_from_tx` emits a fixed event dict with keys eventId/txId/leagueId/ownerId/assetId/assetType/action/txType/ts/week/faabBid — there is no counterpartyUserId key, so `ingest_events` writes NULL every time (`str(event.get('counterpartyUserId') or '') or None`). Runtime confirmation on a 3-team trade: every emitted event's counterparty is None. The platform_ledger trigger therefore always evaluates its NULL branch, and `counterparty_manager_key` is uniformly NULL too. Nothing reads the field for display, so there is no wrong number on screen — but the multi-team-trade question 'who did they trade with' cannot be answered from this store at all, and any future consumer of the column would silently get nothing.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W16/w16_ledger_probe.py | grep -A3 counterparty_present ; grep -n 'counterpartyUserId' src/intel/crawler.py; echo "crawler_matches=$?"
reproduction.expected: crawler emits counterpartyUserId on trade events
reproduction.actual: counterparty_present == ['None']; zero occurrences of counterpartyUserId in crawler.py

userImpact: None today (no reader). The cost is capability: multi-team trades are stored correctly as independent per-owner movements but with no link between the sides, so pair-level analysis (who trades with whom, who is a repeat partner) is impossible without a re-crawl.

priorFinding.note: Not present in the prior A17 set.

whatWorks: Multi-team trades themselves are stored correctly and without double counting (W16-F002); only the linkage between sides is absent.
rootCause: The column and its downstream derivations were added ahead of the crawler field that would fill them.
requiredRepair: For `type=='trade'`, Sleeper supplies `roster_ids`; emit counterpartyUserId when the trade has exactly two rosters and leave it NULL for 3+-team trades (where a single counterparty is not well defined), then backfill nothing — historic rows cannot be recovered.

title: POST /api/intel/refresh is authenticated (session or constant-time bearer) with a per-user cooldown, but any signed-in user can trigger a crawl of EVERY active league
claimUnderTest: 'The refresh + status routes accept EITHER a session cookie or a bearer token ... They are added to the self-authed allowlist so the session-cookie middleware defers to the endpoints' own auth check.'
observed: Verified without POSTing (read-only protocol): anonymous `GET /api/intel/refresh/status` returns 401 auth_required, and a bogus `Authorization: Bearer nope` also returns 401 — so the allowlist entry does not create an anonymous hole. The bearer comparison is `hmac.compare_digest` over UTF-8/surrogateescape bytes (constant-time, and non-ASCII input cannot raise into a 500), rejection logging is rate-limited to one line per 60s and leaks only a length-EQUALITY boolean. Manual triggers carry a 600s per-user cooldown (429 + Retry-After) stamped only after a crawl actually starts; the cron bearer path is exempt by design. The workflow refuses to send the token to a guessed host when PROD_PUBLIC_URL is unset. Residual: authorization is 'any authenticated user', not admin — and `?leagueKey=all` lets any such user start a sequential crawl across every active registry league, i.e. hundreds of budgeted Sleeper calls, once per 10 minutes per account.
userImpact: None directly. The residual risk is resource abuse by an authenticated account against Sleeper's API, bounded by the process crawl lock and the 10-minute cooldown.

priorFinding.note: Prior A17 has no auth finding for the refresh route.

whatWorks: 401 for anonymous and for a wrong bearer; constant-time comparison; rate-limited, secret-length-safe rejection logging; process lock (409) plus per-user cooldown (429) with correct precedence; no hardcoded host in the workflow.
requiredRepair: Optional hardening: gate `?leagueKey=all` on the admin allowlist (bearer/cron unaffected), leaving single-league manual refresh open to any member.

title: Insider Trading is Blocked by data here, but not for the reason the protocol assumes: data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 EXISTS with a full schema and zero rows; what is absent is data/intel/snapshot_dynasty_main.json
claimUnderTest: AUDIT_PROTOCOL non-findings table: '/api/intel/* returns 503 — data/intel/ and the platform ledger DB do not exist in this container'.
observed: `data/intel/` exists and contains `ledger.sqlite3` (319 KB), `ledger.sqlite3.pre-platform-v2-auto.bak` (100 KB) and an `ffpc/` directory. The ledger holds all 19 tables (transactions, asset_movements, canonical_assets, platform_*, sharp_roster_*, manager_seasons, ...) and every one of them has 0 rows except `meta` (3). The 503s are gated on `service.snapshot_ready()`, which is `bool(load_state_cached(key).get('generatedAt'))` — i.e. on the per-league JSON snapshot `data/intel/snapshot_dynasty_main.json`, which does NOT exist. That also explains the route split the workstream was asked about: 5 of 7 routes 503 because they sit behind that gate; `GET /api/intel/refresh/status` is deliberately snapshot-independent and 200s with `snapshotGeneratedAt: null`; `POST /api/intel/leads` returns 400 missing_asset because body validation runs BEFORE the snapshot gate (server.py:12440 precedes 12452). It also explains why the sibling product answers differently: Sharp Tracker reads the ledger directly with no snapshot gate, so it 200s with `status: "cohort_building"` and an all-zero transparency block — an honest empty rather than a refusal.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && ls -la data/intel/ && .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('data/intel/ledger.sqlite3');print([(n,c.execute(f'select count(*) from \"{n}\"').fetchone()[0]) for (n,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table' order by 1\")])" && ls data/intel/snapshot_*.json
reproduction.actual: data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 present, 19 tables, all 0 rows; no snapshot_*.json (ls exits 2)

userImpact: No numeric claim about live intel output can be verified in this container; every finding above was reproduced against synthetic ledgers driven through the real production functions.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed in substance (nothing to verify against) but corrected in fact: the ledger DB does exist and is schema-current; the missing artifact is the per-league snapshot JSON, which is what snapshot_ready() actually gates on.

whatWorks: The 503 body is honest and specific — it names the league key and the exact remedy ('trigger POST /api/intel/refresh or wait for the daily cron') — and every read path degrades rather than raising.
rootCause: No crawl has ever run in this container (correctly — the audit is read-only).
requiredRepair: None. Recorded so the protocol's non-findings table can be corrected.

title: signalStrength, velocity and two of the six allow-listed sorts are computed and shipped on every board row but no UI renders or offers them
claimUnderTest: The API allow-lists six sorts — net, volume, buys, sells, strength, velocity — and the summary route's docstring describes the board as 'sorted by signalStrength'.
observed: `SORT_OPTIONS` in the page offers only net / volume / buys / sells. `grep signalStrength|velocity` over the insider-trading page and InsiderLeads returns nothing, so neither number is displayed even as a column. The two metrics that `signals.py` was written to replace `trendScore` with are therefore computed per row, per window, on every request and discarded by the only consumer.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && grep -n '_INTEL_ALLOWED_SORTS' server.py && grep -n 'SORT_OPTIONS' -A6 frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx && grep -rn 'signalStrength\|velocity' frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx; echo exit=$?
reproduction.actual: UI sorts = net/volume/buys/sells; zero references to signalStrength or velocity

userImpact: The board's headline ordering is raw net, so a 1-buy/0-sell row can outrank a broadly-traded one — exactly the ranking failure signal_strength (direction x sample confidence x breadth) exists to prevent. The user has no way to select it.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed by grep against the live tree; adds the ranking consequence of defaulting to net.

whatWorks: The metrics themselves are sound and the confidence tier IS rendered as a column, so thin rows are at least labelled.
rootCause: UI shipped with a reduced sort set.
requiredRepair: Add Strength and Velocity to SORT_OPTIONS and a Strength column; consider defaulting the board to strength.

title: CLAUDE.md documents none of src/intel/ — a 6,200-line subsystem with seven routes, a page, a daily workflow and two migration scripts — while its shared modules are cited only under Sharp Tracker
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md presents itself as the architecture map of the repo, with a directory tree of src/ and a section per major subsystem.
observed: The `src/` tree in CLAUDE.md lists adapters, api, bdvm, canonical, identity, league_intel, model_registry, scoring, league, trade, data_models, utils — and not `intel/`. The string `src/intel` appears exactly once in the whole file, at line 836, as `src/intel/league_filter.py` inside the SHARP cohort section, i.e. only as an implementation detail of a different product. There is no Insider Trading section, no mention of the intel ledger, the snapshot store, the daily intel-refresh workflow, or the seven routes. By contrast BDVM, Sharp, the trade engines and the valuation overlay each get multi-paragraph treatment. `docs/intel/AUDIT.md` is thorough but is dated 2026-07-29 and still describes the pre-split state as current in places.

reproduction.expected: a subsystem section for Insider Trading
reproduction.actual: one hit: line 836, 'src/intel/league_filter.py' inside the sharp-cohort paragraph

userImpact: An agent or engineer following CLAUDE.md as the map will not know the subsystem exists, will not know the ledger is SHARED with Sharp Tracker, and is one plausible edit away from re-introducing the cohort collapse PR #626 fixed.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed against the current CLAUDE.md at HEAD e96c06ef.

whatWorks: src/intel/__init__.py and docs/intel/AUDIT.md are unusually good in-tree documentation — the gap is only in the file agents are told to trust first.
requiredRepair: Add an 'Insider Trading vs Sharp Tracker' section to CLAUDE.md stating the cohort split, the shared ledger/signals layer, the snapshot gate, and the rule that intel must never import src.sharp.

title: No Next bridge routes exist for /api/intel/*, unlike the sharp and bdvm surfaces — production is unaffected (nginx) but the page cannot be exercised against a dev Next server
claimUnderTest: Comparable subsystems ship dev bridge routes: `frontend/app/api/bdvm/*` and `frontend/app/api/sharp/{cohort,market,roster-percentage}` exist.
observed: `frontend/app/api/intel/` does not exist, so all three intel fetches from the page resolve to Next 404s when the app is loaded from :3000 without a proxy. In production nginx sends `location /api/` to FastAPI so the page works; this is a dev-parity gap, not a production defect, and it is the same topology artifact AUDIT_PROTOCOL warns about. Recorded because it is an inconsistency with the two sibling subsystems, and because it means the intel page is the one Intel/Market surface that cannot be smoke-tested with `npm run dev` alone.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && ls frontend/app/api/sharp frontend/app/api/bdvm ; ls frontend/app/api/intel
reproduction.expected: an intel bridge directory alongside sharp/ and bdvm/
reproduction.actual: sharp/ and bdvm/ exist; ls: cannot access 'frontend/app/api/intel/': No such file or directory

userImpact: None in production. A developer running only the Next dev server sees an intel page that appears broken.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed, with the explicit qualification that production nginx makes this a dev-parity issue rather than a user-facing defect — the prior finding does not say so.

whatWorks: The production path is correct and the page renders fully through request interception (verified live).

title: server.py's intel section header no longer documents the retired trendScore sort — prior finding not reproducible at HEAD
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A17-F13: 'server.py's intel section header still documents the retired trendScore sort'.
observed: `grep -n trendScore server.py` returns nothing at HEAD e96c06ef. The intel section header (server.py:12100-12135) documents the five endpoints, the private-cache posture, the window allow-list ('7d','30d','90d','all') and the sort allow-list ('net','volume','buys','sells','strength','velocity') — no trendScore anywhere. The string survives only in src/intel/signals.py and __init__.py, in both cases as an explicit account of what was REMOVED and why.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && grep -n 'trendScore' server.py; echo exit=$?; grep -rn 'trendScore' src/intel/ --include=*.py
reproduction.expected: per prior finding: a trendScore mention in the server header
reproduction.actual: grep exit=1 in server.py; only historical mentions in src/intel/signals.py and __init__.py

priorFinding.note: Either fixed since the prior audit or mis-scoped in it; at HEAD e96c06ef the claim is false.

whatWorks: The retired formula is documented as retired in exactly one place, with the double-counting arithmetic that justified retiring it.
